transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. After losing a job opportunity I was really counting on, I feel like I’ve been reacting badly to everything and just can’t cope with what’s happening in my life. It feels like everything has just thrown me completely off course.

Do you feel that these overwhelming feelings of worry and low mood started specifically as a direct result of losing that job opportunity, or were you struggling with these symptoms before that event occurred?

Yes, it definitely started right after the job fell through. I was doing totally fine before that, but within a couple of weeks of getting the news, everything just spiraled. Since then, I've found myself completely unable to handle even simple daily tasks.

Since this started, have you noticed that your distress is significantly out of proportion to the severity of losing the job, or that it is causing you major difficulties in your social life or work performance?

Yes, my reaction feels completely out of proportion because even a simple text or email makes my chest tighten, and I just shut my laptop and cry. It's severely affecting my life—I've lost out on paid gigs, stopped going to my regular improv group, and let crucial emails about my lease and student loans pile up.
Has this emotional distress lasted longer than six months since the job loss, or have these symptoms begun to subside as time has passed?

No, it's only been about two months since the job fell through, so it hasn't been six months yet, and the symptoms haven't really started to subside because everything is still so up in the air. However, I really believe this reaction won't go on forever and is just tied to my current unstable situation. Once I can sort out a stable job or a new plan, I think I'll be able to move past this.
